title: Visa Spends 2.4 Billion Dollars to Acquire AI Fraud Prevention Company BioCatch: Analyzing 19 Billion Interactions Per Month to Curb Financial Fraud at the Source
excerpt: Payment giant Visa has announced that it will acquire Israeli artificial intelligence financial fraud prevention company BioCatch for $2.4 billion (approximatel
content_html:
Payment giant Visa has announced that it will acquire Israeli artificial intelligence financial fraud prevention company BioCatch for $2.4 billion (approximately 16.231 billion yuan) in cash, leveraging its behavioral analysis and device intelligence technology to further enhance risk detection capabilities for account theft, financial fraud, dummy accounts, and false account applications. The transaction is currently awaiting regulatory approval and is expected to be completed before the end of Visa's fiscal year 2027, i.e., by the end of March 2027.

Public information shows that BioCatch was founded in 2011 and mainly uses AI and machine learning technologies to analyze behavioral data, device information, application environment, and network signals generated when users access online banking, thereby determining in real-time whether an operation is performed by a genuine user or a potential fraudster. The company currently serves more than 350 financial institutions in 21 countries worldwide, including over 100 large banks. Its system analyzes about 19 billion user interactions each month, covering 760 million users and 1.8 billion devices.

Modeling 3,000 Behavioral Data Points for Comprehensive Risk Detection, Even Identifying "Forced Transfers"

BioCatch's core technology continuously collects more than 3,000 anonymous behavioral data points, including keyboard and mouse operation methods, touch habits, input rhythm, device holding style, whether a jailbroken device is used, and whether there are AI proxy program operations. Its AI model not only verifies account, password, and device information but also analyzes user behavior patterns and operational intent to determine whether the current operator is a genuine user, a fraudster, or a victim being controlled or coerced by others.

For example, if a user suddenly changes their input habits, their device is remotely controlled, or the user is transferring money according to a fraudster's instructions during a call, the system may identify abnormal risks and prompt the bank to perform additional verification or block the transaction. Visa said that after the acquisition, it will move the AI fraud prevention capabilities further upstream from the payment stage, covering user account opening, login, and account operations, and identify potential risks before funds enter Visa's payment network.

AI Speeds Up Fraud, Payment Giants Invest 13 Billion Dollars Over Five Years to Build a Defense

Visa pointed out that account theft and financial fraud cause losses of over 1 trillion dollars to the global economy every year, and the development of generative AI allows hackers to carry out fraud activities faster and on a larger scale. BioCatch's technology will further supplement Visa's existing security, fraud prevention, risk management, and identity verification products, enabling coverage of the entire process from account opening to payment transactions.

In recent years, major payment companies have been expanding their security and anti-fraud capabilities through acquisitions. Visa previously acquired AI fraud detection company Featurespace in 2024, while its competitor Mastercard acquired threat intelligence company Recorded Future for 2.65 billion dollars the same year. Over the past five years, Visa has invested more than 13 billion dollars in building payment security technologies and related infrastructure. As generative AI makes the cost of fraud nearly zero, payment giants are using the same fast-paced acquisition strategy to build a complete defense line from behavioral analysis to transaction interception.

content_html_zh:
支付巨头Visa宣布将以24亿美元（约合162.31亿元人民币）现金收购以色列人工智能金融欺诈防范公司BioCatch，利用其行为分析和设备智能技术，进一步增强对账户盗窃、金融欺诈、虚拟账户、虚假账户申请等风险检测能力。 该交易目前正在等待监管部门批准，预计将在 Visa 2027 财年结束前完成，即 2027 年 3 月结束。

公开资料显示，BioCatch成立于2011年，主要利用人工智能和机器学习技术来分析用户访问网上银行时产生的行为数据、设备信息、应用环境和网络信号，从而实时判断操作是真实用户还是潜在欺诈者。 该公司目前为全球21个国家的350多家金融机构提供服务，其中包括100多家大型银行。 其系统每月分析约 190 亿次用户交互，覆盖 7.6 亿用户和 18 亿台设备。

对 3,000 个行为数据点进行建模以进行全面的风险检测，甚至识别“强制转移”

BioCatch的核心技术持续收集超过3000个匿名行为数据点，包括键盘和鼠标操作方式、触摸习惯、输入节奏、设备握持方式、是否使用越狱设备、是否有AI代理程序操作等。 其AI模型不仅可以验证账户、密码和设备信息，还可以分析用户的行为模式和操作意图，以确定当前操作者是真实用户、欺诈者还是被他人控制或胁迫的受害者。

例如，如果用户突然改变输入习惯、设备被远程控制、或者用户在通话过程中按照诈骗者的指示进行转账，系统可能会识别出异常风险，并提示银行进行额外验证或阻止交易。 Visa表示，收购后，将把AI防欺诈能力从支付阶段进一步向上游延伸，涵盖用户开户、登录和账户操作，并在资金进入Visa支付网络之前识别潜在风险。

AI加速欺诈，支付巨头五年投资130亿美元构筑防御

Visa指出，账户盗窃和金融欺诈每年给全球经济造成超过1万亿美元的损失，而生成式AI的发展使得黑客能够更快、更大规模地开展欺诈活动。 BioCatch的技术将进一步补充Visa现有的安全、欺诈预防、风险管理和身份验证产品，实现从开户到支付交易的全流程覆盖。

近年来，各大支付公司一直通过收购来扩大其安全和反欺诈能力。 Visa此前于2024年收购了人工智能欺诈检测公司Featurespace，而其竞争对手万事达卡则于同年以26.5亿美元收购了威胁情报公司Recorded Future。 过去五年来，Visa已投资超过130亿美元用于建设支付安全技术和相关基础设施。 随着生成式人工智能使欺诈成本接近于零，支付巨头正在使用同样的快节奏收购策略，构建从行为分析到交易拦截的完整防线。
